description: Evaluate how sensitive SCHM's performance is to the choice of threshold tau. Reports hallucination rate and WER for tau in {0.5, 0.6, 0.7} plus boundary conditions (A=never mask, B=always mask).
mode: suppress (output empty transcription when p_nospeech >= tau)

key_findings.hallucination_sensitivity: Hallucination rate varies from 74.37% (tau=0.5) to 81.95% (tau=0.7), a 7.58 pp range. Lower tau suppresses more clips, reducing hallucinations.
key_findings.wer_robustness: WER on LS-clean varies between 2.86% (tau=0.6, 0.7) and 2.95% (tau=0.5). LS-other is constant at 5.10% across all tau -- zero false positives on test-other at all thresholds.
key_findings.false_positive_rate: Very low across all thresholds: 0-2 utterances on LS-clean (0.00-0.08%), 0 on LS-other. The p_nospeech signal cleanly separates speech from non-speech.
key_findings.overall_robustness: SCHM is robust to tau choice in the 0.5-0.7 range. WER cost is negligible (at most +0.12 pp on clean). The main sensitivity is in hallucination reduction: tau=0.5 reduces halluc by 25.6 pp vs default, tau=0.7 by 18.1 pp.
key_findings.pareto_relationship: All SCHM points dominate Condition A (same or better WER, lower hallucination). No SCHM point strictly dominates Condition B on WER (B's WER is 3.08/5.32, SCHM worst is 2.95/5.10 which is better), but B has 100% hallucination (same as A). SCHM is the only condition that reduces hallucination at all.
